blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the rise level, the trial balance is less a check and more a ritual. It is run at the end of each month, before any reports leave the finance team. Every account balance is pulled. Every total is tested against its expected shape. Any anomaly is investigated before the books are closed.

Good teams build a checklist of 'things to look at' that goes beyond the simple debits-equal-credits test. Are the usual zero-balance accounts still zero? Has any account suddenly grown without an explanation? Do the key totals match what the P&L preview is showing?

The trial balance, done properly, is the last quiet line of defence against the numbers being wrong in public. Skipping it is the fastest way to look foolish in a board meeting.

items.q: According to the text, when is the trial balance run?
options: Only when an anomaly is reported
At the end of each month, before any reports leave the team
After the reports have been sent to the board
Once a year, before the audit
items.why: "It is run at the end of each month, before any reports leave the finance team."

items.q: What should a good checklist go beyond?
options: The monthly P&L preview
The simple debits-equal-credits test
The list of zero-balance accounts
The board meeting agenda
items.why: "a checklist… that goes beyond the simple debits-equal-credits test."

items.q: The text calls the trial balance "the last quiet line of defence." This suggests that…
options: it is optional once other checks are done
it is only useful during an audit
it is a noisy, public activity
it is the final safeguard before the numbers become public
items.why: Inferência: "last… line of defence against the numbers being wrong in public" — é a proteção final antes de os números irem a público.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A trial balance is a monthly discipline worth protecting.
Skipping the trial balance carries a real risk.
If debits equal credits, no further checking is needed.
Anomalies should be investigated before the books close.
items.why: Inferência: o texto insiste que o checklist deve ir ALÉM do teste débito = crédito, então o autor discordaria de que basta bater os dois lados.

items.q: What does the author imply about catching problems during the trial balance?
options: It should be left to the auditors
It rarely makes any difference to the final numbers
It is better to find them there than in a board meeting
It is a formality with no real consequence
items.why: Inferência: "Skipping it is the fastest way to look foolish in a board meeting" — pegar o erro no processo evita o vexame público.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily conduzindo o fechamento com um analista júnior. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, let's run the month-end together — I'll talk you through it as we go. First rule: we don't just glance at the totals. The debits and the credits will balance, they nearly always do. That's the easy part. What we're really doing is looking for anything that doesn't fit.

So, pull the full list of account balances and let's walk down it. Now — here. This account. It's a zero-balance account. It should be sitting at nothing, every single month. And it's showing four thousand pounds. See that? That's exactly the kind of thing the debit-equals-credit test will never catch, because the four thousand is balanced somewhere else.

Before we close anything, we investigate that. I'll pull the postings and find out where it came from. Do not close the books with a number you can't explain sitting on the page.

Honestly, this is boring work now, and I know it feels slow. But catching this here, quietly, is nothing. Catching it after the report has gone to the board — that's a very different afternoon. Let's find where the four thousand came from.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Emily say is "the easy part"?
options: Investigating the anomaly
Closing the books
Pulling the list of account balances
The debits and credits balancing
items.why: "The debits and the credits will balance… That's the easy part."

items.q: What is wrong with the account Emily points to?
options: It should be at zero but shows four thousand pounds
It has been closed too early
It is missing from the list entirely
Its debits and credits do not balance
items.why: "It's a zero-balance account… And it's showing four thousand pounds."

items.q: Why does Emily say the debit-equals-credit test won't catch this problem?
options: Because the account is not on the trial balance
Because the four thousand is balanced somewhere else
Because the books are already closed
Because the totals were never pulled
items.why: "the four thousand is balanced somewhere else" — por isso o teste débito = crédito não acusa nada.

items.q: What does Emily mean by "that's a very different afternoon"?
options: Fixing the error after it reaches the board would be far more damaging
The board meeting will be rescheduled
The junior will need to work overtime
The report will take longer to write
items.why: Inferência: contrasta pegar o erro agora (chato, sem consequência) com descobri-lo depois de ir ao board (constrangedor).

items.q: What does the way Emily coaches the junior suggest about her approach?
options: She treats the trial balance as a disciplined, teaching moment
She sees the anomaly as unimportant
She prefers to close the books quickly and fix errors later
She trusts the balancing test to catch every problem
items.why: Inferência: ela explica cada passo, não pula nada e trata o processo como formação — uma disciplina, não uma formalidade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The month-end trial balance is a ritual for the finance team." Here, ritual means…
options: an informal chat
a fixed, disciplined routine performed every time
a religious ceremony
a one-off special event
items.why: Ritual = rotina disciplinada e repetida — não um evento isolado.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Emily asked the junior to pull the full list of account ___ before they started."
options: deadlines
meetings
balances
auditors
items.why: Balance = saldo; pull the balances = extrair os saldos das contas.

items.q: "A previously zero account had grown by £4,000 — a clear anomaly." An anomaly is…
options: a rounding error that can be ignored
a routine, expected figure
a standard monthly adjustment
something that does not fit the expected pattern
items.why: Anomaly = anomalia: algo fora do padrão esperado.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Do not ___ with a number you cannot explain still on the page."
options: pull the balances
build the checklist
close the books
run the preview
items.why: Close the books = fechar os livros; não se deve fechar com um valor sem explicação.

items.q: "Done properly, the trial balance is the last quiet line of defence." This means it is…
options: a list of the team's responsibilities
a physical barrier in the office
the final safeguard against errors reaching the public
a warning sent to the board
items.why: Line of defence = linha de defesa: última proteção antes de os números irem a público.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem no fechamento contábil. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The controller still has to sign off on the trial balance before it's final." To sign off on means to…
options: question it informally
print and file it
formally approve it
delay it to next month
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Let's flag up that £4,000 balance before we go any further." To flag up means to…
options: draw attention to it as needing a look
hide it from the report
delete it from the ledger
approve it quickly
items.why: Flag up = sinalizar, chamar atenção para algo que precisa ser verificado.

items.q: "The junior agreed to look into where the postings came from." To look into means to…
options: investigate carefully
report to the board
approve without checking
ignore for now
items.why: Look into = investigar, examinar a fundo — sinônimo de 'to investigate'.

items.q: "We agreed to check the account, but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
escalated it to the board
documented it in detail
did it twice
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "If the numbers are wrong, an extra checklist item won't paper over the problem." To paper over something means to…
options: document it clearly
escalate it quickly
hide or disguise it without really fixing it
solve it permanently
items.why: Paper over = disfarçar um problema superficialmente, sem resolvê-lo de fato.
